keyVerseText: And it came to pass in the six hundredth and first year, in the first month, the first day of the month, the waters were dried up from off the earth: and Noah removed the covering of the ark, and looked, and, behold, the face of the ground was dry.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew adjective רִאשׁוֹן (riʼshôwn) derives from the root רִאשָׁה (riʼshâh), meaning 'beginning' or 'early time.' This etymology highlights its fundamental sense of something that is first or primary in time or rank. Beyond the English gloss 'first,' the root conveys a sense of origin and precedence, emphasizing not only temporal priority but also foundational status.
usageInScripture: With 182 occurrences, רִאשׁוֹן consistently appears as an adjective describing something that is first, chief, or former, whether in time, place, or rank. The top translations such as 'first,' 'in the first,' and 'the first' reflect its broad but coherent semantic field, emphasizing beginnings, primacy, or precedence. This range shows the word's flexibility in conveying both temporal and hierarchical priority across various contexts in Scripture.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding רִאשׁוֹן as 'first' or 'former' enriches our grasp of biblical revelation by pointing to God's sovereignty over time and order. It underscores God as the origin and initiator of all things, affirming His primacy above creation. This word also invites believers to recognize the importance of beginnings in God's redemptive plan, reminding us that Christ is the 'firstborn' over all creation and the pioneer of salvation. Thus, רִאשׁוֹן deepens our appreciation of God's eternal reign and the unfolding of His purposes from the very start.
keyVerseReflection: In Genesis 8:13, the phrase 'in the first month, the first day of the month' uses רִאשׁוֹן to mark a new beginning after the floodwaters receded. This emphasizes the restoration and renewal of the earth at a divinely appointed time, highlighting God's faithfulness to His covenant and the orderly progression of His plan. The use of רִאשׁוֹן here not only situates the event in time but also symbolizes a fresh start under God's providence.
